questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal once you complete your turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane, what happens?

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
It usually makes it hard for the driver to see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of the lane behind a car places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: In the vehicle's side mirror.
In the vehicle's rearview mirror.
Through the vehicle's passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself behind the car in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror, where they will see you most often.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you ride in when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and helps drivers in the next lane see what you are about to do.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlegrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlegrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlegrips tightly and keep your bike going straight. Only brake if you are sure which tire is flat. Leave the road once the motorcycle has slowed down enough.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, they are required for all riders.
No, but they are recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when turning, entering or leaving a highway, or taking a curve.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires eye protection for all riders on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield offers the best protection.

questions.question: What should passengers do when taking a turn or curve?

options.text: Look over their shoulder in the direction of the turn or curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder in the direction of the turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Before riding, ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps both of you lean the right way.

questions.question: Motorcycles need what stopping distance?

options.text: Less room to stop than larger vehicles.
The same room to stop as larger vehicles.
No stopping distance—they can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same room to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles. Always leave enough space to stop safely based on road conditions.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move to a different lane to give the emergency vehicle more space. Slow down and be ready to stop. Do not stop on the road behind it.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Lean your body in the direction of the turn.
Slow down while in the turn.
Turn by moving only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your body in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Lean into the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because you cannot get used to one lane position.
Discouraged because it confuses other drivers.
Smart when you are adapting to changing road or traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Smart when you are adapting to changing road or traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move around your lane as road and traffic conditions change to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Stay quiet and avoid unnecessary movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay quiet and avoid unnecessary movement.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way.

questions.question: If you refuse to take an alcohol test when an officer asks, your license will be suspended for:

options.text: Three months.
Six months.
12 months.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 months.
questions.explanation: Tennessee law states that by driving, you agree to take an alcohol test if asked. If you refuse, your license will be suspended for 12 months.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should ride in:

options.text: The left side of your lane.
The center of your lane.
The right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This is the safest position. Riding on either side increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means stop. You must stop completely and wait for a green light before you can turn.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The road is slippery.
The sun is shining.
You think stopping will be easy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if the road is slippery. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop safely.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that matches the road and traffic conditions at that moment.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power can cause your rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift immediately to a lower gear.
Proceed in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.
Relax and steer straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven bridge gratings, simply relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even when wearing a helmet. You should wear hearing protection on every ride.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight within your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Changing your path angle may send you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther away from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
Is not encouraged or discouraged as it has no impact on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This may signal the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.
Help you receive wind blasts.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you receive wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your lane position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving because your motorcycle can fall over.

questions.question: A primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while avoiding another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A primary cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. This can cause your motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows the right edge of a traffic lane.
